units.zh: 隋書卷五十二列傳第十七
units.en: Book of Sui, Volume 52, Biographies 17.
units.literal: Book of Sui, Volume 52, Biographies 17.

units.zh: ○韓擒虎弟僧壽洪
units.en: ○ Han Qinhu; his brothers Sengshou and Hong.
units.literal: ○ Han Qinhu; his brothers Sengshou and Hong.

units.zh: 韓擒虎，字子通，河南東垣人也，後家新安。
units.en: Han Qinhu, whose courtesy name was Zitong, came from Dongyuan in Henan; his family later moved to Xin'an.
units.literal: Han Qinhu, courtesy name Zitong, was a native of Dongyuan in Henan; later his family settled in Xin'an.

units.zh: 父雄，以武烈知名，仕周，官至大將軍、洛虞等八州刺史。
units.en: His father Xiong was renowned for martial prowess. He served the Northern Zhou and eventually reached the rank of Grand General and governed eight prefectures, among them Luo and Yu.
units.literal: His father Xiong was famed for martial valor; he served the Zhou and rose to Grand General and governor of eight prefectures including Luo and Yu.

units.zh: 擒虎少慷慨，以膽略見稱，容貌魁岸，有雄傑之表。
units.en: In his youth Qinhu was generous and high-spirited, and won renown for daring and resourcefulness. He was imposing in build and had the look of a great hero.
units.literal: Qinhu in youth was open-handed and bold; he was praised for courage and stratagem, with a towering stature and the bearing of a heroic champion.

units.zh: 性又好書，經史百家皆略知大旨。
units.en: He also loved learning by nature and had a working knowledge of the essential themes of the classics, histories, and the various schools of thought.
units.literal: By nature he also loved books and had a general grasp of the main purport of the classics, histories, and the hundred schools.

units.zh: 周太祖見而異之，令與諸子遊集。
units.en: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou met him, he was struck by the young man's promise and had him keep company with his own sons.
units.literal: Emperor Taizu of Zhou saw him and regarded him as extraordinary, and had him join in the companionship and gatherings of his sons.

units.zh: 後以軍功，拜都督、新安太守，稍遷儀同三司，襲爵新義郡公。
units.en: Later, on the strength of his battlefield record, he was made Area Commander and Administrator of Xin'an, then gradually promoted to Yitong Third Rank and succeeded to the title Duke of Xinyi commandery.
units.literal: Later, through military achievement, he was appointed Area Commander and Administrator of Xin'an; he was gradually promoted to Yitong Third Rank and inherited the title Duke of Xinyi commandery.

units.zh: 武帝伐齊，齊將獨孤永業守金墉城，擒虎說下之。
units.en: When Emperor Wu of Zhou attacked Northern Qi, the Qi general Dugu Yongye held Jinyong. Qinhu talked him into surrendering the city.
units.literal: When Emperor Wu campaigned against Qi, the Qi general Dugu Yongye held Jinyong city; Qinhu persuaded him to submit.

units.zh: 進平范陽，加上儀同，拜永州刺史。
units.en: He went on to pacify Fanyang, was granted the additional rank of Shang Yitong, and was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou.
units.literal: Advancing, he pacified Fanyang, was given the additional rank of Shang Yitong, and was appointed Inspector of Yongzhou.

units.zh: 陳人逼光州，擒虎以行軍總管擊破之。
units.en: When Chen troops pressed Guang Prefecture, Qinhu, serving as Campaign Commander, routed them.
units.literal: When Chen forces pressed Guangzhou, Qinhu as Campaign Commander defeated them.

units.zh: 又從宇文忻平合州。
units.en: He also followed Yuwen Xin in the pacification of Hezhou.
units.literal: He also followed Yuwen Xin in pacifying Hezhou.

units.zh: 高祖作相，遷和州刺史。
units.en: When Yang Jian held the post of Chancellor, Qinhu was transferred to Inspector of Hezhou.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor served as Chancellor, Qinhu was transferred to Inspector of Hezhou.

units.zh: 陳將甄慶、任蠻奴、蕭摩訶等共為聲援，頻寇江北，前後入界。
units.en: The Chen generals Zhen Qing, Ren Man'nu, Xiao Mohe, and others backed one another and raided the north bank of the Yangzi repeatedly, crossing the frontier time after time.
units.literal: The Chen generals Zhen Qing, Ren Man'nu, Xiao Mohe, and others jointly lent each other support and repeatedly raided north of the Yangzi, crossing the border again and again.

units.zh: 擒虎屢挫其鋒，陳人奪氣。
units.en: Qinhu repeatedly broke their momentum, and Chen morale collapsed.
units.literal: Qinhu repeatedly blunted their edge, and the Chen troops lost heart.

units.zh: 開皇初，高祖潛有吞併江南之志，以擒虎有文武才用，夙著聲名，於是拜為廬州總管，委以平陳之任，甚為敵人所憚。
units.en: Early in the Kaihuang reign the emperor quietly set his sights on bringing the south under control. Qinhu was already famed for combining literary and military gifts, so he was made Area Commander of Luzhou and charged with conquering Chen—a commission that struck deep fear into the enemy.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Kaihuang era, the Founding Emperor secretly harbored the aim of swallowing up the lands south of the Yangzi; because Qinhu possessed both civil and military talent and had long been famed, he was appointed Area Commander of Luzhou and entrusted with the task of pacifying Chen, and the enemy feared him greatly.

units.zh: 及大舉伐陳，以擒虎為先鋒。
units.en: When the full-scale invasion of Chen was launched, Qinhu was placed at the head of the army.
units.literal: When a great campaign was launched against Chen, Qinhu was made vanguard.

units.zh: 擒虎率五百人宵濟，襲採石，守者皆醉，擒虎遂取之。
units.en: Qinhu led five hundred men across the river at night and stormed Caishi. The garrison was drunk, and he took the place without difficulty.
units.literal: Qinhu led five hundred men across by night, struck Caishi, the defenders were all drunk, and Qinhu thereupon took it.

units.zh: 進攻姑熟，半日而拔，次於新林。
units.en: He pressed on to Gushu and captured it within half a day, then made camp at Xinlin.
units.literal: He advanced to attack Gushu and took it in half a day, then encamped at Xinlin.

units.zh: 江南父老素聞其威信，來謁軍門，晝夜不絕。
units.en: The elders south of the Yangzi had long known his reputation for authority and fairness. They came to his camp in an unbroken stream, day and night.
units.literal: The elders of the south of the Yangzi had long heard of his prestige and trustworthiness; they came to call at the camp gate day and night without cease.

units.zh: 陳人大駭，其將樊巡、魯世真、田瑞等相繼降之。
units.en: Chen forces were thrown into panic, and generals such as Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, and Tian Rui surrendered to him in succession.
units.literal: The Chen people were greatly alarmed; their generals Fan Xun, Lu Shizhen, Tian Rui, and others surrendered to him one after another.

units.zh: 晉王廣上狀，高祖聞而大悅，宴賜群臣。
units.en: Prince Jin Guang reported the news upstream. The emperor was delighted and held a feast to reward his ministers.
units.literal: Prince of Jin Guang submitted a memorial; when the Founding Emperor heard it he was greatly pleased and held a feast to reward the court ministers.

units.zh: 晉王遣行軍總管杜彥與擒虎合軍，步騎二萬，陳叔寶遣領軍蔡徵守朱雀航，聞擒虎將至，眾懼而潰。
units.en: The Prince of Jin sent Campaign Commander Du Yan to join Qinhu with twenty thousand foot and horse. Chen Shubao ordered Palace Guard Director Cai Zheng to hold the Zhuque crossing, but at word that Qinhu was approaching the army panicked and broke.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin sent Campaign Commander Du Yan to join forces with Qinhu—twenty thousand infantry and cavalry. Chen Shubao sent the Director of the Palace Guard Cai Zheng to hold the Zhuque crossing; when they heard Qinhu was coming, the troops were afraid and scattered in rout.

units.zh: 任蠻奴為賀若弼所敗，棄軍降於擒虎。
units.en: Ren Man'nu, already beaten by He Ruobi, abandoned his troops and surrendered to Qinhu.
units.literal: Ren Man'nu had been defeated by He Ruobi; he abandoned his army and surrendered to Qinhu.

units.zh: 擒虎以精騎五百，直入硃雀門。
units.en: Qinhu rode through the Zhuque Gate at the head of five hundred elite cavalry.
units.literal: Qinhu with five hundred picked horsemen entered straight through the Zhuque Gate.

units.zh: 陳人欲戰，蠻奴捴之曰：「老夫尚降，諸君何事！」
units.en: The Chen soldiers were ready to fight, but Man'nu shouted them down: "If even I, an old man, have surrendered, what are you still fighting for!"
units.literal: The Chen troops wished to fight; Man'nu rebuked them, saying, "Even I, an old man, have submitted—what business have you!"

units.zh: 眾皆散走。
units.en: The men broke and fled in all directions.
units.literal: The crowd all scattered and fled.

units.zh: 遂平金陵，執陳主叔寶。
units.en: He then took Jinling and captured Chen's ruler, Shubao.
units.literal: Thereupon he pacified Jinling and seized Chen's ruler Shubao.

units.zh: 時賀若弼亦有功。
units.en: He Ruobi had won distinction as well.
units.literal: At that time He Ruobi also had merit.

units.zh: 乃下詔于晉王曰：「此二公者，深謀大略，東南逋寇，朕本委之，靜地恤民，悉如朕意。
units.en: The emperor then issued an edict to the Prince of Jin: "These two commanders planned with foresight and executed on a grand scale. I entrusted the unruly southeast to them, and in calming the country and caring for the people they have done exactly as I intended.
units.literal: Thereupon an edict was issued to the Prince of Jin, saying, "These two lords possess deep counsel and grand strategy. The fugitive bandits of the southeast—I originally entrusted them to them; in pacifying the land and showing compassion to the people, all has been as I wished.

units.zh: 九州不一，已數百年，以名臣之功，成太平之業，天下盛事，何用過此！
units.en: The realm had been divided for centuries; through the service of such renowned ministers the work of unification and peace has been achieved. What triumph under Heaven could be greater than this!
units.literal: The Nine Provinces have not been united for several hundred years; through the achievement of famed ministers, the work of great peace has been accomplished—what event under Heaven could surpass this!

units.zh: 聞以欣然，實深慶快。
units.en: To hear this news fills me with joy; my satisfaction is profound.
units.literal: On hearing it I am pleased with joy; truly my celebration and delight are deep.

units.zh: 平定江表，二人之力也。」
units.en: The pacification of the south is the work of these two men alone."
units.literal: The pacification of the lands along the Yangzi is the achievement of these two men."

units.zh: 賜物萬段。
units.en: Each was rewarded with ten thousand bales of goods.
units.literal: They were granted ten thousand bales of goods.

units.zh: 又下優詔於擒虎、弼曰：「申國威于萬里，宣朝化於一隅，使東南之民俱出湯火，數百年寇旬日廓清，專是公之功也。
units.en: A special edict went out to Qinhu and Bi: "You have carried our might across the realm and brought the court's civilizing rule to a distant quarter, lifting the people of the southeast out of misery. Centuries of disorder were swept away in days—and that is your doing alone.
units.literal: A gracious edict was also issued to Qinhu and Bi, saying, "You have displayed the state's might for ten thousand li and spread the court's transforming influence in a corner of the realm, so that the people of the southeast all escaped boiling water and raging fire; banditry of several hundred years was cleared in the space of days—this achievement is yours alone.

units.zh: 高名塞于宇宙，盛業光於天壤，逖聽前古，罕聞其匹。
units.en: Your renown fills heaven and earth; your achievement outshines the land. Search the records of antiquity as you will—you will seldom find your equal.
units.literal: Your lofty fame fills the cosmos; your splendid achievement shines between heaven and earth. Listening far back into antiquity, one rarely hears its equal.

units.zh: 班師凱入，誠知非遠，相思之甚，寸陰若歲。」
units.en: Your victorious return cannot be far away. I miss you so keenly that every moment drags like a year."
units.literal: Your triumphant return with the army cannot, I know, be far off; my longing for you is so deep that each inch of shadow is like a year."

units.zh: 及至京，弼與擒虎爭功於上前，弼曰：「臣在蔣山死戰，破其銳卒，擒其驍將，震揚威武，遂平陳國。
units.en: After they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu argued over credit before the emperor. Bi said, "I fought to the death on Mount Jiang, shattered their elite forces, captured their boldest generals, and by that display of force brought Chen to its knees.
units.literal: When they reached the capital, Bi and Qinhu disputed merit before the throne. Bi said, "Your servant fought to the death on Mount Jiang, broke their crack troops, captured their fierce generals, displayed awe-inspiring might, and thereby pacified the state of Chen.

units.zh: 韓擒虎略不交陣，豈臣之比！」
units.en: Han Qinhu barely drew sword—how can he stand comparison with me!"
units.literal: Han Qinhu scarcely crossed spears at all—how can he be compared with your servant!"

units.zh: 擒虎曰：「本奉明旨，令臣與弼同時合勢，以取偽都。
units.en: Qinhu replied, "I was under your explicit orders to coordinate with Bi and strike the rebel capital together.
units.literal: Qinhu said, "I originally received your clear command that your servant and Bi should combine our strength at the same time to take the false capital.

units.zh: 弼乃敢先期，逢賊遂戰，致令將士傷死甚多。
units.en: Yet Bi rushed ahead on his own, met the enemy, and fought prematurely, costing us many dead and wounded.
units.literal: Bi dared to move ahead of schedule; when he met the enemy he fought at once, causing many officers and soldiers to be wounded and killed.

units.zh: 臣以輕騎五百，兵不血刃，直取金陵，降任蠻奴，執陳叔寶，據其府庫，傾其巢穴。
units.en: I took five hundred light cavalry, entered Jinling without shedding blood, received Ren Man'nu's surrender, seized Chen Shubao, and occupied the treasuries and the heart of their power.
units.literal: Your servant with five hundred light horsemen, blades unstained with blood, took Jinling straight off, made Ren Man'nu submit, seized Chen Shubao, occupied their treasuries, and overturned their nest.

units.zh: 弼至夕，方扣北掖門，臣啟關而納之。
units.en: Bi did not reach the North Side Gate until evening; I was the one who opened the gate and let him in.
units.literal: Bi only in the evening came to knock at the North Side Gate; your servant opened the gate and admitted him.

units.zh: 斯乃救罪不暇，安得與臣相比！」
units.en: He was lucky to escape blame—how can he compare with me!"
units.literal: He had barely time to beg off his offenses—how could he be compared with your servant!"

units.zh: 上曰：「二將俱合上勳。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Both of you have earned the highest credit."
units.literal: The emperor said, "Both generals alike merit supreme merit."

units.zh: 於是進位上柱國，賜物八千段。
units.en: Qinhu was then promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and given eight thousand bales of goods.
units.literal: Thereupon Qinhu was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and granted eight thousand bales of goods.

units.zh: 有司劾擒虎放縱士卒，淫汙陳宮，坐此不加爵邑。
units.en: The authorities charged Qinhu with allowing his troops to run riot and desecrate the Chen palace, and for that reason he received no further titles or fiefs.
units.literal: The responsible offices impeached Qinhu for letting his soldiers run wild and defiling the Chen palace; on this account he was not given additional enfeoffment or fief.

units.zh: 先是，江東有謠歌曰：「黃斑青驄馬，發自壽陽涘。
units.en: Earlier a song had circulated east of the Yangzi: "A yellow-spotted gray horse, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.
units.literal: Earlier, in the lands east of the Yangzi there had been a ballad saying, "A yellow-spotted blue-gray horse, setting out from the banks of Shouyang.

units.zh: 來時冬氣末，去日春風始。」
units.en: It came as winter was ending; it left as spring was beginning."
units.literal: When it came, winter's breath was ending; when it went, spring wind was beginning."

units.zh: 皆不知所謂。
units.en: No one understood what it meant.
units.literal: No one knew what it meant.

units.zh: 擒虎本名豹，平陳之際，又乘青驄馬，往反時節與歌相應，至是方悟。
units.en: Qinhu had been born with the name Bao, "Leopard"; during the conquest of Chen he again rode a gray horse, and the timing of his campaign matched the ballad—only then did people see its meaning.
units.literal: Qinhu's original name was Bao [Leopard]; at the time of pacifying Chen he again rode a blue-gray horse, and the seasons of his going and returning corresponded to the song—only then did people understand.

units.zh: 其後突厥來朝，上謂之曰：「汝聞江南有陳國天子乎？」
units.en: Later, when Turkish envoys came to court, the emperor asked them, "Have you heard of the Chen emperor south of the Yangzi?"
units.literal: Later, when the Turks came to court, the emperor said to them, "Have you heard that south of the Yangzi there was an emperor of the state of Chen?"

units.zh: 對曰：「聞之。」
units.en: They answered, "We have."
units.literal: They replied, "We have heard of him."

units.zh: 上命左右引突厥詣擒虎前，曰：「此是執得陳國天子者。」
units.en: The emperor had attendants bring the Turks before Qinhu and said, "This is the man who took the Chen emperor prisoner."
units.literal: The emperor ordered attendants to lead the Turks before Qinhu and said, "This is the man who captured the emperor of Chen."

units.zh: 擒虎厲然顧之，突厥惶恐，不敢仰視，其有威容如此。
units.en: Qinhu fixed them with a fierce glare. The Turks trembled and dared not look up—such was the force of his presence.
units.literal: Qinhu turned on them with a stern look; the Turks were afraid and did not dare raise their eyes—such was the majesty of his bearing.

units.zh: 別封壽光縣公，食邑千戶。
units.en: He received a separate enfeoffment as Duke of Shouguang county with a fief of one thousand households.
units.literal: He was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Shouguang county with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 以行軍總管屯金城，禦備胡寇，即拜涼州總管。
units.en: As Campaign Commander he garrisoned Jincheng against northern raids and was promptly appointed Area Commander of Liangzhou.
units.literal: As Campaign Commander he was stationed at Jincheng to guard against barbarian raiders, and was at once appointed Area Commander of Liangzhou.

units.zh: 俄征還京，上宴之內殿，恩禮殊厚。
units.en: He was soon recalled to the capital, where the emperor entertained him in the inner palace with extraordinary honor.
units.literal: Soon he was summoned back to the capital; the emperor feasted him in the inner hall with exceptional favor and courtesy.

units.zh: 無何，其鄰母見擒虎門下儀衛甚盛，有同王者，母異而問之。
units.en: Not long after, a neighbor woman saw such a royal display of guards and banners at Qinhu's gate that she asked in astonishment what it meant.
units.literal: Before long, a neighboring woman saw under Qinhu's gate guards and insignia so grand they were like a king's; surprised, the woman asked about it.

units.zh: 其中人曰：「我來迎王。」
units.en: One of the figures said, "I have come to welcome the king."
units.literal: Someone among them said, "I have come to welcome the king."

units.zh: 忽然不見。
units.en: Then they vanished.
units.literal: Suddenly they were gone.

units.zh: 又有人疾篤，忽驚走至擒虎家曰：「我欲謁王。」
units.en: Another man, deathly ill, suddenly leapt up and ran to Qinhu's house crying, "I must pay my respects to the king."
units.literal: Again, a man gravely ill suddenly started up and ran to Qinhu's house, saying, "I wish to pay court to the king."

units.zh: 左右問曰：「何王也？」
units.en: His attendants asked, "Which king?"
units.literal: Those beside him asked, "What king?"

units.zh: 答曰：「閻羅王。」
units.en: He answered, "King Yama."
units.literal: He answered, "King Yama."

units.zh: 擒虎子弟欲撻之，擒虎止之曰：「生為上柱國，死作閻羅王，斯亦足矣。」
units.en: Qinhu's sons wanted to beat the man, but Qinhu stopped them. "Supreme Pillar of State in life, King Yama in death—that is glory enough," he said.
units.literal: Qinhu's sons and younger relatives wished to flog the man; Qinhu stopped them, saying, "Alive as Supreme Pillar of State, dead as King Yama—that is enough."

units.zh: 因寢疾，數日竟卒，時年五十五。
units.en: He fell ill shortly afterward and died within days, at the age of fifty-five.
units.literal: He then took to his bed with illness and after several days died at last, aged fifty-five.

units.zh: 子世諤嗣。
units.en: His son Shi'e succeeded to his line.
units.literal: His son Shi'e succeeded him.

units.zh: 世諤倜儻驍捷，有父風。
units.en: Shi'e was daring, quick, and unconventional, very much in his father's mold.
units.literal: Shi'e was free-spirited, bold, and swift, and had his father's manner.

units.zh: 楊玄感之作亂也，引世諤為將，每戰先登。
units.en: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he enlisted Shi'e as a commander, and in every battle Shi'e was the first over the wall.
units.literal: When Yang Xuangan raised rebellion, he drew Shi'e in as a general; in every battle Shi'e was first to scale the walls.

units.zh: 及玄感敗，為吏所拘。
units.en: When Xuangan was crushed, the authorities seized him.
units.literal: When Xuangan was defeated, Shi'e was seized by the officials.

units.zh: 時帝在高陽，送詣行所。
units.en: The emperor was at Gaoyang, and Shi'e was sent to him there.
units.literal: The emperor was then at Gaoyang; Shi'e was sent to the traveling court.

units.zh: 世諤曰令守者市酒殽以酣暢，揚言曰：「吾死在朝夕，不醉何為！」
units.en: Shi'e persuaded his guards to buy wine and a feast and proclaimed aloud, "I am as good as dead—why not drink while I still can!"
units.literal: Shi'e had the guards buy wine and food for a hearty carouse, and proclaimed aloud, "My death is at hand from morning to night—if I do not get drunk, what shall I do!"

units.zh: 漸以酒進守者，守者狎之，遂飲令致醉。
units.en: He kept pressing wine on the guards until they grew careless, drank freely, and passed out drunk.
units.literal: Gradually he offered wine to the guards; they grew familiar with him and drank until he made them drunk.

units.zh: 世諤因得逃奔山賊，不知所終。
units.en: Shi'e escaped and joined the mountain rebels; nothing more is known of his fate.
units.literal: Shi'e thereby escaped and fled to mountain bandits; his end is unknown.

units.zh: 僧壽字玄慶，擒虎母弟也，亦以勇烈知名。
units.en: Sengshou, whose courtesy name was Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger uterine brother and was likewise renowned for martial valor.
units.literal: Sengshou, courtesy name Xuanqing, was Qinhu's younger brother by the same mother; he too was famed for courage and fierceness.

units.zh: 周武帝時，為侍伯中旅下大夫。
units.en: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he served as Lower Grand Master of the Central Brigade of the Palace Guard.
units.literal: Under Emperor Wu of Zhou he was Lower Grand Master of the Central Brigade of the Palace Guard.

units.zh: 高祖得政，從韋孝寬平尉迥，每戰有功，授大將軍，封昌樂公，邑千戶。
units.en: When Yang Jian took control of the government, Sengshou followed Wei Xiaokuan against Yu Chi and distinguished himself in every engagement. He was made Grand General and enfeoffed as Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor seized power, Sengshou followed Wei Xiaokuan in pacifying Yu Chi; in every battle he had merit, was appointed Grand General, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Changle with a fief of one thousand households.

units.zh: 開皇初，拜安州刺史。
units.en: Early in the Kaihuang reign he was appointed Inspector of Anzhou.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Inspector of Anzhou.

units.zh: 時擒虎為廬州總管，朝廷不欲同在淮南，轉為熊州刺史。
units.en: Qinhu was then Area Commander of Luzhou, and the court did not want both brothers in Huainan at once, so Sengshou was moved to Inspector of Xiongzhou.
units.literal: At that time Qinhu was Area Commander of Luzhou; the court did not wish the two brothers together in Huainan, so Sengshou was transferred to Inspector of Xiongzhou.

units.zh: 後轉蔚州刺史，進爵廣陵郡公。
units.en: He was later transferred to Inspector of Weizhou and promoted to Duke of Guangling commandery.
units.literal: Later he was transferred to Inspector of Weizhou and advanced in rank to Duke of Guangling commandery.

units.zh: 尋以行軍總管擊突厥于雞頭山，破之。
units.en: Soon afterward, as Campaign Commander, he attacked the Turks at Jitou Mountain and routed them.
units.literal: Soon, as Campaign Commander, he attacked the Turks at Jitou Mountain and defeated them.

units.zh: 後坐事免。
units.en: He was later dismissed after being implicated in an offense.
units.literal: Later he was dismissed because of an offense.

units.zh: 數歲，複拜蔚州刺史。
units.en: Several years later he was reappointed Inspector of Weizhou.
units.literal: After several years he was again appointed Inspector of Weizhou.

units.zh: 突厥甚憚之。
units.en: The Turks held him in deep dread.
units.literal: The Turks feared him greatly.

units.zh: 十七年，屯蘭州以備胡。
units.en: In the seventeenth year of the reign he garrisoned Lanzhou against the northern peoples.
units.literal: In the seventeenth year he was stationed at Lanzhou to guard against the barbarians.

units.zh: 明年，遼東之役，領行軍總管，還，檢校靈州總管事。
units.en: The following year he served as Campaign Commander in the Liaodong expedition. On his return he was made acting Area Commander of Lingzhou.
units.literal: The next year, in the Liaodong campaign, he led as Campaign Commander; on his return he was made acting Area Commander of Lingzhou.

units.zh: 從楊素擊突厥，破之，進位上柱國，改封江都郡公。
units.en: He joined Yang Su against the Turks, won a victory, was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State, and was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Jiangdu commandery.
units.literal: He followed Yang Su in striking the Turks and defeated them; he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jiangdu commandery.

units.zh: 煬帝即位，又改封新蔡郡公。
units.en: When Emperor Yang came to the throne, his title was changed again to Duke of Xincai commandery.
units.literal: When Emperor Yang acceded, his title was again changed to Duke of Xincai commandery.

units.zh: 自是之後，不復任用。
units.en: After that he was never again given office.
units.literal: From then on he was no longer employed.

units.zh: 大業五年，從幸太原。
units.en: In the fifth year of Daye he accompanied the emperor to Taiyuan.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Daye he accompanied the imperial progress to Taiyuan.

units.zh: 有京兆人達奚通妾王氏，能清歌，朝臣多相會觀之，僧壽亦豫焉，坐是除名。
units.en: A concubine of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao named Wang was famed for her refined singing. Many ministers gathered to hear her, and Sengshou joined them; for that he was dismissed from office.
units.literal: There was a concubine Wang of Daxi Tong of Jingzhao who could sing pure songs; many court ministers gathered to watch her, and Sengshou also took part—on this account he was struck from the rolls.

units.zh: 尋令復位。
units.en: He was soon restored to office.
units.literal: Soon he was ordered restored to his post.

units.zh: 八年，卒于京師，時年六十五。
units.en: In the eighth year he died in the capital at the age of sixty-five.
units.literal: In the eighth year he died in the capital, aged sixty-five.

units.zh: 有子孝基。
units.en: He left a son, Xiaoji.
units.literal: He had a son Xiaoji.

units.zh: 洪字叔明，擒虎季弟也。
units.en: Hong, whose courtesy name was Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.
units.literal: Hong, courtesy name Shuming, was Qinhu's youngest brother.

units.zh: 少驍勇，善射，膂力過人。
units.en: In his youth he was bold and fierce, an expert archer, and stronger than ordinary men.
units.literal: In youth he was fierce and brave, skilled in archery, and his physical strength surpassed other men.

units.zh: 仕周侍伯上士，後以軍功拜大都督。
units.en: He served the Northern Zhou as Senior Gentleman of the Palace Guard and later became Grand Commander on the strength of his battlefield record.
units.literal: He served the Zhou as Senior Gentleman of the Palace Guard; later, through military achievement, he was appointed Grand Commander.

units.zh: 高祖為丞相，從韋孝寬破尉迥於相州，加上開府，甘棠縣侯，邑八百戶。
units.en: While Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Hong followed Wei Xiaokuan in the defeat of Yu Chi at Xiangzhou, was granted the additional title of Opening the Mansion, and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Gantang county with eight hundred households.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor was Chancellor, Hong followed Wei Xiaokuan in defeating Yu Chi at Xiangzhou, was given the additional office of Opening the Mansion, and was made Marquis of Gantang county with a fief of eight hundred households.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，進爵為公。
units.en: When Yang Jian took the throne, Hong was promoted to duke.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, Hong was advanced in rank to duke.

units.zh: 尋授驃騎將軍。
units.en: He was soon appointed General of Valiant Cavalry.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed General of Valiant Cavalry.

units.zh: 開皇九年，平陳之役，授行軍總管。
units.en: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, during the conquest of Chen, he was made Campaign Commander.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang, in the campaign to pacify Chen, he was appointed Campaign Commander.

units.zh: 及陳平，晉王廣大獵于蔣山，有猛獸在圍中，眾皆懼。
units.en: After Chen fell, Prince Jin Guang staged a grand hunt on Mount Jiang. A savage beast broke into the ring, and everyone was terrified.
units.literal: When Chen was pacified, the Prince of Jin Guang held a great hunt on Mount Jiang; a fierce beast was within the encirclement, and all were afraid.

units.zh: 洪馳馬射之，應弦而倒。
units.en: Hong spurred his horse forward, loosed an arrow, and the beast dropped at the bow's report.
units.literal: Hong galloped on horseback and shot it; at the twang of the bowstring it fell.

units.zh: 陳氏諸將，列觀於側，莫不歎伏焉。
units.en: Chen's former generals stood in a row to watch, every one of them sighing with admiration.
units.literal: The various generals of the Chen clan lined up to watch from the side, and none failed to sigh in admiration and submit in awe.

units.zh: 王大喜，賜縑百匹。
units.en: The prince was delighted and rewarded him with a hundred bolts of silk.
units.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and granted him one hundred bolts of silk.

units.zh: 尋以功加柱國，拜蔣州刺史。
units.en: Shortly afterward his battlefield record earned him the rank of Pillar of State and appointment as Inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Soon, through achievement, he was given the additional rank of Pillar of State and appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 數歲，轉廉州刺史。
units.en: A few years later he was reassigned as Inspector of Lianzhou.
units.literal: After several years he was transferred to Inspector of Lianzhou.

units.zh: 時突厥屢為邊患，朝廷以洪驍勇，檢校朔州總管事。
units.en: The Turks were raiding the frontier with growing frequency, and the court, trusting in Hong's martial prowess, put him in charge of Shuozhou as acting area commander.
units.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly became a border affliction; because Hong was fierce and brave, the court made him acting Area Commander of Shuozhou.

units.zh: 尋拜代州總管。
units.en: He was soon formally appointed Area Commander of Daizhou.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed Area Commander of Daizhou.

units.zh: 仁壽元年，突厥達頭可汗犯塞，洪率蔚州刺史劉隆、大將軍李藥王拒之。
units.en: In the first year of Renshou, the Turk khan Datou broke through the border. Hong marched out with Liu Long, Inspector of Weizhou, and the great general Li Yaowang to meet him.
units.literal: In the first year of Renshou, the Turkic khan Datou invaded the frontier passes; Hong led Liu Long, Inspector of Weizhou, and the great general Li Yaowang to resist him.

units.zh: 遇虜于恆安，眾寡不敵，洪四面搏戰，身被重創，將士沮氣。
units.en: At Heng'an they met the enemy badly outnumbered. Hong fought on every side, took grave wounds, and his troops' spirits sank.
units.literal: They encountered the enemy at Heng'an; their numbers could not match the foe's; Hong fought on all four sides, his body suffered grave wounds, and officers and soldiers lost heart.

units.zh: 虜悉眾圍之，矢下如雨。
units.en: The Turks massed their full strength around them, and arrows came down like rain.
units.literal: The enemy gathered their entire force to surround them; arrows fell like rain.

units.zh: 洪偽與虜和，圍少解。
units.en: Hong pretended to negotiate peace, and the ring of besiegers slackened slightly.
units.literal: Hong feigned making peace with the enemy, and the encirclement loosened somewhat.

units.zh: 洪率所領潰圍而出，死者大半，殺虜亦倍。
units.en: Hong led his men in a desperate breakout. More than half his force was lost, but they killed twice as many of the enemy.
units.literal: Hong led those under his command in breaking out of the encirclement; more than half died, yet those they killed among the enemy were twice as many.

units.zh: 洪及藥王除名為民，隆竟坐死。
units.en: Hong and Li Yaowang were stripped of rank and reduced to commoners; Liu Long was eventually sentenced to death.
units.literal: Hong and Yaowang were stripped of rank and made commoners; Long in the end was condemned and executed.

units.zh: 煬帝北巡，至恆安，見白骨被野，以問侍臣。
units.en: On a northern tour Emperor Yang came to Heng'an, saw bleached bones strewn across the fields, and asked his attendants about them.
units.literal: Emperor Yang toured the north; when he reached Heng'an and saw white bones covering the wilds, he questioned his attending ministers.

units.zh: 侍臣曰：「往者韓洪與虜戰處也。」
units.en: An attendant replied, "This is the ground where Han Hong once fought the Turks."
units.literal: A minister attending him said, "This is where Han Hong fought the barbarians of old."

units.zh: 帝憫然傷之，收葬骸骨，命五郡沙門為設佛供，拜洪隴西太守。
units.en: Moved to pity, the emperor had the bones gathered and buried, ordered monks from five commanderies to perform Buddhist rites, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.
units.literal: The emperor sighed in pity and grief, gathered and buried the bones, ordered Buddhist monks of five commanderies to set out Buddhist offerings, and appointed Hong Administrator of Longxi.

units.zh: 未幾，硃崖民王萬昌作亂，詔洪擊平之。
units.en: Before long Wang Wanchang of Zhuyai raised a rebellion, and Hong was ordered to crush it.
units.literal: Before long, Wang Wanchang of Zhuyai commandery raised rebellion; an edict ordered Hong to attack and pacify him.

units.zh: 以功加位金紫光祿大夫，領郡如故。
units.en: For this success he was promoted to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon while retaining his prefectural post.
units.literal: Through achievement his rank was raised to Grand Master of Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, and he retained his commandery as before.

units.zh: 俄而萬昌弟仲通複叛，又詔洪討平之。
units.en: Soon Wanchang's brother Zhongtong rebelled as well, and Hong was again sent to put him down.
units.literal: Soon Wanchang's younger brother Zhongtong rebelled again; again an edict ordered Hong to suppress and pacify him.

units.zh: 師未旋，遇疾而卒，時年六十三。
units.en: His army had not yet returned when illness took him. He was sixty-three.
units.literal: Before the army returned, he fell ill and died, aged sixty-three at the time.

units.zh: ○賀若弼
units.en: ○ He Ruo Bi
units.literal: ○ He Ruo Bi

units.zh: 賀若弼，字輔伯，河南洛陽人也。
units.en: He Ruo Bi, whose courtesy name was Fubo, came from Luoyang in Henan.
units.literal: He Ruo Bi, courtesy name Fubo, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

units.zh: 父敦，以武烈知名，仕周為金州總管，宇文護忌而害之。
units.en: His father Dun was renowned for martial prowess. He had served the Northern Zhou as Area Commander of Jinzhou until Yuwen Hu, envying him, had him put to death.
units.literal: His father Dun was famed for martial valor; he served the Zhou as Area Commander of Jinzhou, but Yuwen Hu, envying him, had him killed.

units.zh: 臨刑，呼弼謂之曰：「吾必欲平江南，然此心不果，汝當成吾志。
units.en: At the execution block he called Bi to him and said, "I always meant to bring Jiangnan under control, but that ambition will die with me. You must finish what I began.
units.literal: Facing execution, he called Bi and said to him, "I have always wished to pacify Jiangnan, yet this heart's aim will not be fulfilled—you must accomplish my aspiration.

units.zh: 且吾以舌死，汝不可不思。」
units.en: And I am dying for my own loose tongue. Do not forget that lesson."
units.literal: Moreover, I die because of my tongue—you must not fail to reflect on this."

units.zh: 因引錐刺弼舌出血，誡以慎口。
units.en: He then drove an awl through Bi's tongue until it bled, warning him to guard every word he spoke.
units.literal: Thereupon he took an awl and pierced Bi's tongue until it bled, admonishing him to be careful with his mouth.

units.zh: 弼少慷慨有大志，驍勇便弓馬，解屬文，博涉書記，有重名於當世。
units.en: In youth Bi was open-handed and ambitious, fierce in battle and expert with bow and horse, able to compose prose, widely read in the histories, and widely respected in his own day.
units.literal: Bi in youth was magnanimous and possessed a great aspiration; he was fierce and brave, skilled with bow and horse, adept at composing literary pieces, broadly versed in written records, and had heavy renown in his age.

units.zh: 周齊王憲聞而敬之，引為記室。
units.en: Prince Xian of Northern Zhou heard of him, held him in esteem, and made him a secretariat secretary.
units.literal: Prince Xian of Qi of Zhou heard of him and treated him with respect, bringing him in as a secretariat attendant.

units.zh: 未幾，封當亭縣公，遷小內史。
units.en: He was soon enfeoffed as Duke of Dangting county and promoted to Junior Inner Scribe.
units.literal: Before long he was enfeoffed as Duke of Dangting county and transferred to Junior Inner Scribe.

units.zh: 周武帝時，上柱國烏丸軌言於帝曰：「太子非帝王器，臣亦嘗與賀若弼論之。」
units.en: During the reign of Northern Zhou's Emperor Wu, Supreme Pillar of State Wuwan Gui told the emperor, "The crown prince is no emperor's material. I have discussed this with He Ruo Bi as well."
units.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou, Supreme Pillar of State Wuwan Gui said to the emperor, "The crown prince is not material for an emperor; your subject has also once discussed this with He Ruo Bi."

units.zh: 帝呼弼問之，弼知太子不可動搖，恐禍及己，詭對曰：「皇太子德業日新，未睹其闕。」
units.en: The emperor summoned Bi and questioned him. Bi knew the crown prince's position could not be moved and feared for his own life, so he evasively answered, "The crown prince's virtue grows by the day. I have seen no flaw in him."
units.literal: The emperor summoned Bi and questioned him; Bi knew the crown prince could not be shaken, feared calamity reaching himself, and deceitfully replied, "The crown prince's virtue and achievement renew themselves daily; I have not seen his failings."

units.zh: 帝默然。
units.en: The emperor said nothing.
units.literal: The emperor was silent.

units.zh: 弼既退，軌讓其背己，弼曰：「君不密則失臣，臣不密則失身，所以不敢輕議也。」
units.en: After Bi withdrew, Gui reproached him for going back on their understanding. Bi said, "When a ruler is indiscreet he loses his minister; when a minister is indiscreet he loses his life. That is why I would not speak openly."
units.literal: When Bi had withdrawn, Gui reproached him for betraying him; Bi said, "If the ruler is not discreet he loses his minister; if the minister is not discreet he loses his life—therefore I did not dare lightly discuss it."

units.zh: 及宣帝嗣位，軌竟見誅，弼乃獲免。
units.en: When Emperor Xuan came to the throne, Gui was eventually executed—and Bi was spared.
units.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded to the throne, Gui in the end was put to death, and Bi thereby escaped harm.

units.zh: 尋與韋孝寬伐陳，攻拔數十城，弼計居多。
units.en: He soon joined Wei Xiaokuan in the campaign against Chen, helped capture dozens of cities, and most of the plans behind those victories were Bi's.
units.literal: Soon he joined Wei Xiaokuan in campaigning against Chen, stormed and took several tens of cities, and Bi's stratagems predominated in most cases.

units.zh: 拜夀州刺史，改封襄邑縣公。
units.en: He was appointed Inspector of Shouzhou and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyi county.
units.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Shouzhou and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Xiangyi county.

units.zh: 高祖為丞相，尉迥作亂鄴城，恐弼為變，遣長孫平馳驛代之。
units.en: While Yang Jian was still Chancellor, Yu Chi rebelled at Yecheng. Fearing Bi might turn traitor, he sent Changsun Ping by fast relay to relieve him of command.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor was Chancellor, Yu Chi raised rebellion at Yecheng; fearing Bi might change sides, he sent Changsun Ping post-haste by relay stations to replace him.

units.zh: 高祖受禪，陰有並江南之志，訪可任者。
units.en: After Yang Jian took the throne he quietly set his mind on unifying the south and asked whom he could trust with the task.
units.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the abdication, he secretly harbored the aim of swallowing Jiangnan and sought one who could be entrusted with the task.

units.zh: 高熲曰：「朝臣之內，文武才幹，無若賀若弼者。」
units.en: Gao Jiong answered, "Among the ministers, no one matches He Ruo Bi in combined civil and military talent."
units.literal: Gao Jiong said, "Among the court ministers, in civil and military talent and capacity, there is none like He Ruo Bi."

units.zh: 高祖曰：「公得之矣。」
units.en: The emperor said, "You have named the right man."
units.literal: The Founding Emperor said, "You have got it exactly."

units.zh: 於是拜弼為吳州總管，委以平陳之事，弼忻然以為己任。
units.en: Bi was then made Area Commander of Wuzhou and charged with conquering Chen—a mission he accepted with evident satisfaction.
units.literal: Thereupon Bi was appointed Area Commander of Wuzhou and entrusted with the matter of pacifying Chen; Bi gladly took it as his own charge.

units.zh: 與壽州總管源雄並為重鎮。
units.en: He and Yuan Xiong at Shouzhou together anchored the empire's southern front.
units.literal: He and Yuan Xiong, Area Commander of Shouzhou, together formed a pair of great strongholds.

units.zh: 弼遺雄詩曰：「交河驃騎幕，合浦伏波營，勿使騏驎上，無我二人名。」
units.en: Bi sent Yuan Xiong a verse: "The flying-cavalry pavilion at Jiaohe, Fubo's camp at Hepu—when glory mounts the qilin's back, let not our two names be missing from the roll."
units.literal: Bi sent Yuan Xiong a poem saying, "The camp of the Flying Cavalry at Jiaohe, the encampment of Fubo at Hepu—let not the qilin's back bear accolades without our two names upon it."

units.zh: 獻取陳十策，上稱善，賜以寶刀。
units.en: He submitted ten stratagems for the conquest of Chen. The emperor approved them and gave him a treasured sword.
units.literal: He presented ten stratagems for taking Chen; the emperor praised them and granted him a precious blade.

units.zh: 開皇九年，大舉伐陳，以弼為行軍總管。
units.en: In the ninth year of Kaihuang the empire launched a full-scale invasion of Chen, with Bi as Campaign Commander.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Kaihuang a great campaign was launched against Chen, with Bi as Campaign Commander.

units.zh: 將渡江，酹酒而咒曰：「弼親承廟略，遠振國威，伐罪吊民，除凶翦暴，上天長江，鑒其若此。
units.en: Before crossing the Yangzi he poured wine as an offering and swore an oath: "I take the court's grand design upon myself, carry our nation's might to distant shores, punish the guilty and succor the people, root out evil and end tyranny—Heaven and the Yangzi are my witnesses.
units.literal: About to cross the river, he poured a libation and swore, saying, "Bi personally receives the court's grand strategy, bears the state's prestige to distant lands, punishes guilt and comforts the people, removes the vicious and cuts down the violent—Heaven above and the Yangzi bear witness to this.

units.zh: 如便福善禍淫，大軍利涉；
units.en: If Heaven truly rewards virtue and punishes wickedness, may this army cross in safety;
units.literal: If indeed fortune attends the good and calamity the vicious, may the great army cross in ease;

units.zh: 如事有乖違，得葬江魚腹中，死且不恨。」
units.en: but if fate turns against us, let me lie in the bellies of the Yangzi's fish—I will die without regret."
units.literal: if affairs go against this, let me be buried in the bellies of the river fish—I shall die without regret."

units.zh: 先是，弼請緣江防人每交代之際，必集曆陽。
units.en: Earlier Bi had arranged that whenever the Yangzi garrison forces rotated duty, they must muster at Liyang.
units.literal: Before this, Bi had requested that each time the river-guard garrisons changed duty they must assemble at Liyang.

units.zh: 於是大列旗幟，營幕被野。
units.en: He then planted banners on a massive scale until tents and pennants covered the fields.
units.literal: Thereupon he arrayed banners and flags on a great scale, and camp pavilions covered the wilds.

units.zh: 陳人以為大兵至，悉發國中士馬。
units.en: The Chen court believed a full invasion was at hand and mobilized every soldier and horse in the realm.
units.literal: The Chen people thought a great army had arrived and mustered all the troops and horses in the realm.

units.zh: 既知防人交代，其眾複散。
units.en: Once they realized it was only a routine rotation, the armies dispersed again.
units.literal: When they learned it was only the garrison changing duty, their masses again dispersed.

units.zh: 後以為常，不復設備。
units.en: After that they treated such alarms as routine and stopped preparing defenses.
units.literal: Later this was taken as routine, and they no longer made preparations.

units.zh: 及此，弼以大軍濟江，陳人弗之覺也。
units.en: This time Bi crossed the Yangzi with his full army, and the Chen never noticed.
units.literal: On this occasion Bi led the great army across the river, and the Chen people did not perceive it.

units.zh: 襲陳南徐州，拔之，執其刺史黃恪。
units.en: He struck Southern Xuzhou by surprise, took the city, and captured its inspector, Huang Ke.
units.literal: He surprised Chen's Southern Xuzhou, stormed it, and seized its Inspector Huang Ke.

units.zh: 軍令嚴肅，秋毫不犯。
units.en: Discipline in his army was iron—not even a stalk of grain was touched.
units.literal: Military discipline was severe; not even an autumn hair was violated.

units.zh: 有軍士于民間沽酒者，弼立斬之。
units.en: When a soldier was caught buying wine in town, Bi had him executed on the spot.
units.literal: When a soldier bought wine among the people, Bi at once had him beheaded.

units.zh: 進屯蔣山之白土岡，陳將魯達、周智安、任蠻奴、田瑞、樊毅、孔范、蕭摩訶等以勁兵拒戰。
units.en: He advanced to Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang, where Chen's generals Lu Da, Zhou Zhi'an, Ren Man'nu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe, and others barred his path with elite troops.
units.literal: Advancing, he encamped at Baitu Hill on Mount Jiang; the Chen generals Lu Da, Zhou Zhi'an, Ren Man'nu, Tian Rui, Fan Yi, Kong Fan, Xiao Mohe, and others met him with crack troops in battle.

units.zh: 田瑞先犯弼軍，弼擊走之。
units.en: Tian Rui attacked first; Bi drove him off.
units.literal: Tian Rui first attacked Bi's army; Bi struck and put him to flight.

units.zh: 魯達等相繼遞進，弼軍屢卻。
units.en: Lu Da and the rest pressed forward one after another, and Bi's line gave ground again and again.
units.literal: Lu Da and the others in succession advanced wave upon wave, and Bi's army repeatedly fell back.

units.zh: 弼揣知其驕，士卒且惰，於是督厲將士，殊死戰，遂大破之。
units.en: Bi judged the enemy overconfident and his own men growing slack. He rallied his officers and men to a fight to the death and broke the Chen army completely.
units.literal: Bi surmised that they were arrogant and his own troops were growing slack; thereupon he spurred and exhorted officers and soldiers to fight a battle unto death, and in the end routed them utterly.

units.zh: 麾下開府員明擒摩訶至，弼命左右牽斬之。
units.en: His officer Yuan Ming, holder of the title Opening the Mansion, brought Xiao Mohe as a captive. Bi ordered his guards to drag him out for execution.
units.literal: His subordinate Kaifu Yuan Ming captured Mohe and brought him; Bi ordered those at his side to drag him forth and behead him.

units.zh: 摩訶顏色自若，弼釋而禮之。
units.en: Mohe's face never changed. Bi released him and received him with full courtesy.
units.literal: Mohe's countenance remained as calm as before; Bi released him and treated him with ceremony.

units.zh: 從北掖門而入。
units.en: He entered the city through the North Side Gate.
units.literal: He entered by the North Side Gate.

units.zh: 時韓擒虎已執陳叔寶，弼至，呼叔寶視之。
units.en: By then Han Qinhu had already taken Chen Shubao prisoner. When Bi arrived he summoned Shubao to face him.
units.literal: At that time Han Qinhu had already seized Chen Shubao; when Bi arrived he called Shubao forth to look at him.

units.zh: 叔寶惶懼流汗，股慄再拜。
units.en: Shubao broke out in a cold sweat, his legs trembling as he kowtowed again and again.
units.literal: Shubao was fearful and alarmed, sweating; his legs trembling, he bowed twice.

units.zh: 弼謂之曰：「小國之君，當大國卿，拜，禮也。
units.en: Bi told him, "A ruler of a lesser state greeting an officer of a greater one—that bow is proper etiquette.
units.literal: Bi said to him, "The ruler of a small state meeting a minister of a great state—bowing is proper ritual.

units.zh: 入朝不失作歸命侯，無勞恐懼。」
units.en: When you appear at court you will still be made Marquis Who Surrenders. There is nothing to fear."
units.literal: When you enter court you will not lose the making of a Marquis Who Submits to Fate—there is no need for fear."

units.zh: 既而弼恚恨不獲叔寶，功在韓擒虎之後，於是與擒虎相詢，挺刃而出。
units.en: Afterward Bi brooded over having missed capturing Shubao himself and taking second place to Han Qinhu. He quarreled with Qinhu and went for his blade.
units.literal: Soon afterward Bi resented and regretted that he had not captured Shubao himself, that his merit stood after Han Qinhu's; thereupon he exchanged words with Qinhu and, drawing a blade, came forth.

units.zh: 上聞弼有功，大悅，下詔褒揚，語在《韓擒虎傳》。
units.en: When the emperor heard of Bi's success he was delighted and issued an edict of praise; the full account appears in the biography of Han Qinhu.
units.literal: The emperor heard that Bi had merit, was greatly pleased, and issued an edict praising and commending him—the account is in the "Biography of Han Qinhu."

units.zh: 晉王以弼先期決戰，違軍命，於是以弼屬吏。
units.en: Prince Jin Guang, angry that Bi had forced a decisive battle ahead of schedule in defiance of orders, handed him over to the military judges.
units.literal: The Prince of Jin, because Bi had decided the battle ahead of schedule in violation of military orders, thereupon turned Bi over to the legal officers.

units.zh: 上驛召之，及見，迎勞曰：「克定三吳，公之功也。
units.en: The emperor summoned him by fast courier. When they met, he welcomed him with praise: "Pacifying the Three Wu was your doing.
units.literal: The emperor summoned him by post relay; when he arrived and was received, the emperor greeted him with praise, saying, "The pacification of Sanwu is your achievement.

units.zh: 命登禦坐，賜物八千段，加位上柱國，進爵宋國公，真食襄邑三千戶，加以寶劍、寶帶、金甕、金盤各一，並雉尾扇、曲蓋，雜彩二千段，女樂二部，又賜陳叔寶妹為妾。」
units.en: Have him take a seat beside the throne and shower him with rewards: eight thousand bales of goods, promotion to Supreme Pillar of State, elevation to Duke of Song, a fief of three thousand households at Xiangyi, a precious sword, belt, golden jar, and golden platter, pheasant-tail fans and curved canopies, two thousand bales of colored silk, two bands of palace musicians, and Chen Shubao's younger sister as concubine."
units.literal: He ordered him to ascend the imperial seat, granted eight thousand bales of goods, promoted him to Supreme Pillar of State, advanced his noble rank to Duke of Song state, granted a fief income of three thousand households at Xiangyi, and further gave him each one of a precious sword, precious belt, golden jar, and golden platter, along with pheasant-tail fans, curved canopies, two thousand bales of mixed silks, two troupes of female musicians, and also granted him Chen Shubao's younger sister as concubine."

units.zh: 拜右領軍大將軍，尋轉右武候大將軍。
units.en: He was made General of the Right Army of the Guard, then transferred to General of the Right Military Guard.
units.literal: He was appointed General of the Right Army of the Guard; soon he was transferred to General of the Right Military Guard.

units.zh: 弼時貴盛，位望隆重，其兄隆為武都郡公，弟東為萬榮郡公，並刺史、列將。
units.en: Bi was then at the height of power and prestige. His elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu and his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong; all held prefectures and field commands.
units.literal: At that time Bi was illustrious and flourishing, his position and repute weighty and solemn; his elder brother Long was Duke of Wudu commandery, his younger brother Dong Duke of Wanrong commandery—all were prefectural governors and ranked generals.

units.zh: 弼家珍玩不可勝計，婢妾曳綺羅者數百，時人榮之。
units.en: Bi's household overflowed with treasures, and hundreds of maidservants and concubines dressed in silks; contemporaries regarded his station as the summit of honor.
units.literal: The precious curios in Bi's household were beyond counting; serving girls and concubines trailing gauze and silk numbered in the hundreds, and men of the time envied him for it.

units.zh: 弼自謂功名出朝臣之右，每以宰相自許。
units.en: Bi believed his achievements outranked every minister at court and openly expected to be made chancellor.
units.literal: Bi considered his merit and fame to stand above the court ministers, and often reckoned himself fit for the chancellorship.

units.zh: 既而楊素為右僕射，弼仍為將軍，甚不平，形於言色，由是免官，弼怨望愈甚。
units.en: When Yang Su became Right Vice Director while Bi remained only a general, Bi's displeasure showed plainly in words and face. He was stripped of office, and his resentment only deepened.
units.literal: Before long Yang Su became Right Vice Director; Bi remained a general, was very displeased, and it showed in word and countenance; on this account he was dismissed from office, and Bi's resentment grew ever deeper.

units.zh: 後數年，下弼獄，上謂之曰：「我以高熲、楊素為宰相，汝每倡言，雲此二人惟堪啖飯耳，是何意也？」
units.en: A few years later Bi was thrown into prison. The emperor confronted him: "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su my chancellors, yet you kept saying they were fit for nothing but filling their bowls. What did you mean by that?"
units.literal: Several years later Bi was cast into prison; the emperor said to him, "I made Gao Jiong and Yang Su chancellors, yet you repeatedly spread word saying these two men are fit only for eating rice—what is the meaning of this?"

units.zh: 弼曰：「熲，臣之故人，素，臣之舅子，臣並知其為人，誠有此語。」
units.en: Bi replied, "Jiong is an old friend of mine, and Su is my nephew by marriage. I know both men well, and I did say it."
units.literal: Bi said, "Jiong is an old acquaintance of your subject; Su is my nephew by marriage—I know both their characters, and I truly did speak such words."

units.zh: 公卿奏弼怨望，罪當死。
units.en: The officials reported that Bi's resentful talk amounted to a capital crime.
units.literal: The dukes and ministers memorialized that Bi harbored resentment, and his offense deserved death.

units.zh: 上惜其功，於是除名為民。
units.en: The emperor valued his past service, however, and reduced him to commoner status instead of executing him.
units.literal: The emperor prized his achievements, and thereupon stripped him of rank and made him a commoner.

units.zh: 歲餘，複其爵位。
units.en: After a year his titles were restored.
units.literal: After more than a year his noble rank and position were restored.

units.zh: 上亦忌之，不復任使，然每宴賜，遇之甚厚。
units.en: The emperor still mistrusted him and gave him no further appointments, yet at every banquet and grant he treated Bi with unusual generosity.
units.literal: The emperor also feared him and no longer appointed or employed him, yet whenever there were feasts and grants he treated him with great munificence.

units.zh: 開皇十九年，上幸仁壽宮，宴王公，詔弼為五言詩，詞意憤怨，帝覽而容之。
units.en: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor feasted the princes at Renshou Palace and ordered Bi to compose a pentasyllabic poem. The verses were bitter and resentful, but the emperor let them pass.
units.literal: In the nineteenth year of Kaihuang the emperor visited Renshou Palace, feasted the princes and dukes, and ordered Bi to compose a five-character poem; the words and intent were resentful and bitter, yet when the emperor read it he tolerated it.

units.zh: 嘗遇突厥入朝，上賜之射，突厥一發中的。
units.en: On one occasion when Turks came to court, the emperor arranged an archery display. A Turk hit the target on his first shot.
units.literal: Once when Turks came to court, the emperor granted them an archery contest; a Turk hit the target with one shot.

units.zh: 上曰：「非賀若弼無能當此。」
units.en: The emperor said, "Only He Ruo Bi can answer this."
units.literal: The emperor said, "None but He Ruo Bi can meet this challenge."

units.zh: 於是命弼。
units.en: He then summoned Bi.
units.literal: Thereupon he ordered Bi.

units.zh: 弼再拜祝曰：「臣若赤誠奉國者，當一發破的。
units.en: Bi bowed twice and prayed aloud: "If I serve the state with a loyal heart, let my first arrow find the mark.
units.literal: Bi twice bowed and prayed, saying, "If your subject is one who serves the state with pure loyalty, let one shot pierce the target.

units.zh: 如其不然，發不中也。」
units.en: If not, let the arrow miss."
units.literal: If it is not so, the shot will not hit."

units.zh: 既射，一發而中。
units.en: He loosed one arrow—and hit.
units.literal: Having shot, with one release he hit.

units.zh: 上大悅，顧謂突厥曰：「此人天賜我也！」
units.en: The emperor was delighted and said to the Turks, "Heaven gave me this man!"
units.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and, turning to the Turks, said, "This man Heaven has given to me!"

units.zh: 煬帝之在東宮，嘗謂弼曰：「楊素、韓擒虎、史萬歲三人，俱稱良將，優劣如何？」
units.en: While he was still crown prince, Emperor Yang once asked Bi, "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui are all called great generals—how do they rank against one another?"
units.literal: When Emperor Yang was in the Eastern Palace, he once said to Bi, "Yang Su, Han Qinhu, and Shi Wansui—the three are all called fine generals; how do they compare in superiority and inferiority?"

units.zh: 弼曰：「楊素是猛將，非謀將；
units.en: Bi answered, "Yang Su is a fierce fighter, not a strategist;
units.literal: Bi said, "Yang Su is a fierce general, not a stratagem general;

units.zh: 韓擒虎是鬥將，非領將；
units.en: Han Qinhu is a duelist, not a commander;
units.literal: Han Qinhu is a combat general, not a command general;

units.zh: 史萬歲是騎將，非大將。」
units.en: Shi Wansui is a cavalryman, not a supreme commander."
units.literal: Shi Wansui is a cavalry general, not a great general."

units.zh: 太子曰：「然則大將誰也？」
units.en: The crown prince asked, "Then who is the supreme commander?"
units.literal: The crown prince said, "Then who is the great general?"

units.zh: 弼拜曰：「唯殿下所擇。」
units.en: Bi bowed and said, "That is for Your Highness to decide."
units.literal: Bi bowed and said, "Whomever Your Highness selects."

units.zh: 弼意自許為大將。
units.en: In his own mind, Bi was already the supreme commander.
units.literal: In his mind Bi took himself to be the great general.

units.zh: 及煬帝嗣位，尤被疏忌。
units.en: Once Emperor Yang took the throne, Bi was kept at an even greater distance and watched with suspicion.
units.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded to the throne, Bi was especially kept at a distance and regarded with suspicion.

units.zh: 大業三年，從駕北巡，至榆林。
units.en: In the third year of Daye he joined the emperor's northern tour as far as Yulin.
units.literal: In the third year of Daye he accompanied the imperial progress on the northern tour as far as Yulin.

units.zh: 帝時為大帳，其下可坐數千人，召突厥啟民可汗饗之。
units.en: The emperor pitched an enormous tent that could seat thousands and summoned Qimin Qaghan of the Turks to a feast beneath it.
units.literal: The emperor had at that time a great tent under which several thousand men could be seated; he summoned Qimin Qaghan of the Turks to feast there.

units.zh: 弼以為大侈，與高熲、宇文弼等私議得失，為人所奏，竟坐誅，時年六十四。
units.en: Bi considered the display outrageously lavish and privately debated its folly with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and others. Someone informed on them, and Bi was executed at the age of sixty-four.
units.literal: Bi regarded this as gross extravagance and privately discussed its right and wrong with Gao Jiong, Yuwen Bi, and others; someone reported them, and in the end Bi was executed on the charge, aged sixty-four.

units.zh: 妻子為官奴婢，群從徙邊。
units.en: His wife and children were enslaved to the state, and his kinsmen were exiled to the borderlands.
units.literal: His wife and children were made government slave-servants, and his clansmen were banished to the frontier.

units.zh: 子懷亮，慷慨有父風，以柱國世子拜儀同三司。
units.en: His son Huailiang was generous and spirited like his father and, as heir to a Pillar of State, was appointed Yitong Third Rank.
units.literal: His son Huailiang was open-handed and had his father's manner; as heir of a Pillar of State he was appointed Yitong Third Rank.

units.zh: 坐弼為奴，俄亦誅死。
units.en: Implicated in his father's fall, he was enslaved and soon executed as well.
units.literal: Because of Bi's punishment he was made a slave; soon he too was executed.

units.zh: 史臣曰：夫天地未泰，聖哲啟其機；
units.en: The historiographer writes: When heaven and earth are not yet at peace, sages and worthies seize the moment;
units.literal: The historiographer says: When heaven and earth are not yet at peace, sages and worthies open the opportunity;

units.zh: 疆埸尚梗，爪牙宣其力。
units.en: when the frontiers remain blocked, warriors and champions bring their strength to bear.
units.literal: when the frontiers are still obstructed, talons and fangs display their strength.

units.zh: 周之方、邵，漢室韓、彭，代有其人，非一時也。
units.en: Zhou had its Fang and Shao; the Han had its Han Xin and Peng Yue. Every age produces such men—it is never a matter of one moment alone.
units.literal: The Fang and Shao of Zhou, the Han and Peng of the Han house—each age has had such men; it is not a matter of one time alone.

units.zh: 自晉衰微，中原幅裂，區宇分隔，將三百年。
units.en: From the decline of Jin the heartland was torn apart and the realm sundered—for nearly three hundred years.
units.literal: From the decline of Jin, the central plains were torn apart and the realm divided—for nearly three hundred years.

units.zh: 陳氏憑長江之地險，恃金陵之餘氣，以為天限南北，人莫能窺。
units.en: The Chen court trusted in the Yangzi's natural defenses and Jinling's residual prestige, believing heaven itself had divided north from south and that no foe could cross.
units.literal: The house of Chen relied on the Yangzi's strategic terrain and trusted in Jinling's lingering vigor, believing that heaven had set north and south apart and that no man could peer across.

units.zh: 高祖爰應千齡，將一函夏。
units.en: The Founding Emperor answered the summons of the age and set out to reunite the realm.
units.literal: The Founding Emperor then answered the call of a thousand years and was about to unify all within the four seas.

units.zh: 賀若弼慷慨，申必取之長策，韓擒虎奮發，賈餘勇以爭先，勢甚疾雷，鋒逾駭電。
units.en: He Ruobi, bold and high-spirited, laid out the strategy that would surely win; Han Qinhu threw himself into the fight and spent his last reserves of daring to lead the charge. Their momentum was like thunder, their blades swifter than lightning.
units.literal: He Ruobi was open-handed and bold, setting forth the long strategy that must seize victory; Han Qinhu roused himself and sold his remaining courage to race ahead—their momentum like sudden thunder, their edge surpassing startling lightning.

units.zh: 隋氏自此一戎，威加四海。
units.en: With this single campaign the Sui made their might felt across the four seas.
units.literal: From this one campaign the house of Sui made its authority felt across the four seas.

units.zh: 稽諸天道，或時有廢興，考之人謀，實二臣之力。
units.en: Measured against heaven's way, dynasties rise and fall in their season; measured by human design, the conquest was truly the work of these two ministers.
units.literal: Examined against the way of heaven, rise and fall come in their seasons; examined in human counsel, it was truly the power of these two ministers.

units.zh: 其俶儻英略，賀若居多，武毅威雄，韓擒虎稱重。
units.en: In daring strategy and sweeping design, He Ruo had the edge; in martial resolve and commanding presence, Han Qinhu was the greater name.
units.literal: In bold unconventionality and heroic strategy, He Ruo had the greater share; in martial resolve and awe-inspiring might, Han Qinhu was the weightier name.

units.zh: 方于晉之王、杜，勳庸綽有餘地。
units.en: Set beside the Wang and Du of Jin, their achievements would still have stood with room to spare.
units.literal: Compared with Jin's Wang and Du, their achievements and merit still had room to spare.

units.zh: 然賀若功成名立，矜伐不已，竟顛殞於非命，亦不密以失身。
units.en: Yet He Ruo, once his fame was won, never stopped boasting of it and in the end died an untimely death—he had also failed to guard his tongue and paid with his life.
units.literal: Yet He Ruo, his merit and fame established, never ceased boasting of his achievements; in the end he toppled and perished by an untimely death—he had also failed to keep counsel and so lost his life.

units.zh: 若念父臨終之言，必不及於斯禍矣。
units.en: Had he remembered his father's dying warning, he would never have come to such ruin.
units.literal: Had he kept his father's dying words in mind, he would surely not have reached this calamity.

units.zh: 韓擒虎累世將家，威聲動俗，敵國既破，名遂身全，幸也。
units.en: Han Qinhu came from generations of military houses, and his reputation shook the realm. Once the enemy state fell, he won lasting fame and kept his life—a piece of good fortune.
units.literal: Han Qinhu came from a family of generals for generations; his awesome reputation shook the age. Once the enemy state was broken, his fame was achieved and his person preserved—fortunate indeed.

units.zh: 廣陵、甘棠，鹹有武藝，驍雄膽略，並為當時所推，赳赳干城，難兄難弟矣。
units.en: The dukes of Guangling and Gantang were both skilled in arms; in boldness and resource they were admired alike—fierce bulwarks of the state, brothers each the equal of the other.
units.literal: The lords of Guangling and Gantang both had martial arts; in fierce valor and daring stratagem they were alike commended in their day—stalwart defenders of the realm, brothers hard to match one against the other.

units.zh: 是時，隋將韓擒虎及賀若弼等已濟江據蔣山，慧紀聞之，留其長史陳文盛等居守，身率將士三萬人，樓船千餘乘，沿江而下，欲趣臺城。
units.en: By then Sui generals Han Qihu, He Ruobi, and others had already crossed the river and seized Jiangshan. On hearing this, Huiji left his chief clerk Chen Wensheng and others to hold his post and personally led thirty thousand troops in more than a thousand tower ships downriver, intending to reach Taicheng.
units.literal: At this time the Sui generals Han Qihu and He Ruobi and others had already crossed the river and seized Jiangshan; when Huiji heard of it, he left his Chief Clerk Chen Wensheng and others to hold the defense and personally led thirty thousand officers and soldiers in more than a thousand tower ships downstream, intending to hurry to Taicheng.

units.zh: 從子持節、員外散騎常侍、明威將軍、雍州刺史、監南徐州擬，持節、通直散騎侍郎、貞威將軍、北徐州刺史褒，從子晃、炅，從孫假節、員外散騎常侍、明威將軍訬，假節、信威將軍、北徐州刺史吉陽縣開國侯諠，假節、通直散騎侍郎、信武將軍祏，[1]假節、散騎侍郎、雄信將軍、青州刺史、廣梁太守詳，貞威將軍、通直散騎侍郎慧紀，從孫敬雅、敬泰，並枝戚密近，劬勞王室，宜列河山，以光利建。
units.en: His nephew Ni, holder of the staff, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, general of illustrious prestige, prefect of Yongzhou, and supervisor of Southern Xuzhou; Bao, holder of the staff, palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, general of upright prestige, and prefect of Northern Xuzhou; the nephews Huang and Jiong; the great-nephew Xu, acting holder of the staff, supernumerary attendant-in-ordinary of the scattered cavalry, and general of illustrious prestige; Xuan, acting holder of the staff, general of trustworthy prestige, prefect of Northern Xuzhou, and marquis of Jiyang county; Zhi, acting holder of the staff, palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry, and general of trustworthy martiality;[1] Xiang, acting holder of the staff, palace gentleman of the scattered cavalry, general of majestic trust, prefect of Qingzhou, and administrator of Guangliang; Huiji, general of upright prestige and palace gentleman of regular attendance of the scattered cavalry; and the great-nephews Jingya and Jingtai—all close collateral kin who have labored for the royal house—should be granted domains upon the rivers and mountains to honor the founding of the dynasty.
units.literal: The Founder's nephew, Holder of the Staff, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Illustrious Prestige, Prefect of Yongzhou, and Supervisor of Southern Xuzhou, Ni; the Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Upright Prestige, and Prefect of Northern Xuzhou, Bao; the nephews Huang and Jiong; the great-nephew, Acting Holder of the Staff, Supernumerary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Cavalry, and General of Illustrious Prestige, Xu; the Acting Holder of the Staff, General of Trustworthy Prestige, Prefect of Northern Xuzhou, and Marquis of Jiyang County, Xuan; the Acting Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, and General of Trustworthy Martiality, Zhi;[1] the Acting Holder of the Staff, Palace Gentleman of the Scattered Cavalry, General of Majestic Trust, Prefect of Qingzhou, and Administrator of Guangliang, Xiang; General of Upright Prestige and Palace Gentleman of Regular Attendance of the Scattered Cavalry, Huiji; and the great-nephews Jingya and Jingtai—all collateral kin of close degree who have toiled for the royal house—ought to be arrayed among the rivers and mountains to brighten the founding of the state.

units.zh: 及隋師濟江，元帥清河公楊素下自巴硤，慧紀遣其將呂忠肅、陸倫等拒之，[4]戰敗，素進據馬頭。
units.en: When Sui forces crossed the Yangzi, the commander-in-chief, Duke of Qinghe Yang Su, came down from Baxia; Huiji sent his generals Lü Zhongsu, Lu Lun, and others to oppose them,[4] but they were defeated and Su advanced to seize Matou.
units.literal: When the Sui army crossed the Yangzi, the commander-in-chief, the Duke of Qinghe Yang Su, descended from Baxia; Huiji sent his generals Lü Zhongsu, Lu Lun, and others to resist them;[4] they were defeated in battle, and Su advanced and seized Matou.

units.zh: 至漢口，為秦王軍所拒，不得進，因與湘州刺史晉熙王叔文、巴州刺史畢寶等請降。
units.en: At Hankou he was blocked by the army of the Prince of Qin and could not advance; he therefore joined Shuwen, prince of Jinxi and prefect of Xiangzhou, Bi Bao, prefect of Bazhou, and others in offering surrender.
units.literal: Reaching Hankou, he was blocked by the Prince of Qin's army and could not advance; he therefore joined the Prefect of Xiangzhou, the Prince of Jinxi Xiao Shuwen, the Prefect of Bazhou Bi Bao, and others in requesting surrender.

units.zh: 蕭巋授皎司空，巴州刺史戴僧朔，衡陽內史任蠻奴，巴陵內史潘智虔，岳陽太守章昭裕，
units.en: Xiao Kui made Jiao minister of works and set Dai Sengshuo over Ba, Ren Mannu over Hengyang, Pan Zhiquan over Baling, and Zhang Zhaoyu over Yueyang;
units.literal: Xiao Kui appointed Jiao Minister of Works; Dai Sengshuo, Administrator of Ba; Ren Mannu, Interior Minister of Hengyang; Pan Zhiquan, Interior Minister of Baling; Zhang Zhaoyu, Administrator of Yueyang;

units.zh: 皎黨曹慶、錢明、潘智虔、魯閑、席慧略等四十餘人並誅，唯任蠻奴、章昭裕、曹宣、劉廣業獲免。
units.en: Jiao's followers Cao Qing, Qian Ming, Pan Zhiquan, Lu Xian, Xi Huilüe, and more than forty others were put to death; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were pardoned.
units.literal: Jiao's partisans Cao Qing, Qian Ming, Pan Zhiquan, Lu Xian, Xi Huilüe, and more than forty others were all executed; only Ren Mannu, Zhang Zhaoyu, Cao Xuan, and Liu Guangye were spared.

units.zh: 庚戌，以柱國常山公于翼、化政公宇文忻竝為上柱國。
units.en: On gengxu day Pillar-of-State Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and Yuwen Xin, Duke of Huazheng, were both made superior pillars-of-state.
units.literal: On gengxu day Pillar-of-State Yu Yi, Duke of Changshan, and Yuwen Xin, Duke of Huazheng, were both made superior pillars-of-state.

units.zh: 進封翼為任國公，忻為英國公。
units.en: Yu Yi was promoted to Duke of Ren; Yuwen Xin was promoted to Duke of Ying.
units.literal: Yu Yi was advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Ren; Yuwen Xin was advanced to Duke of Ying.

units.zh: 楊玄感之反也，玄感弟玄縱自帝所逃赴其兄，路逢綝。
units.en: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Xuangan's brother Xuanzong fled the imperial camp to join him and met Shen on the road.
units.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Xuangan's younger brother Xuanzong escaped from the emperor's side to join his elder brother and encountered Shen on the road.

units.zh: 壬子，以大將軍、安城公憲為益州總管。
units.en: On renzi day Grand General Yuwen Xian, Duke of Ancheng, was made governor-general of Yi Province.
units.literal: On day renzi, Grand General, Duke of Ancheng Yuwen Xian was made governor-general of Yi Province.

units.zh: 辛未，進封輔城公邕為魯國公，安城公憲為齊國公，秦郡公直為衛國公，正平公招為趙國公。
units.en: On xinwei day Yuwen Yong, Duke of Fucheng, was promoted to Duke of Lu; Yuwen Xian of Ancheng to Duke of Qi; Yuwen Zhi of Qin commandery to Duke of Wei; and Yuwen Zhao of Zhengping to Duke of Zhao.
units.literal: On day xinwei, Duke of Fucheng Yuwen Yong was advanced to Duke of Lu State, Duke of Ancheng Yuwen Xian to Duke of Qi State, Duke of Qin Commandery Yuwen Zhi to Duke of Wei State, Duke of Zhengping Yuwen Zhao to Duke of Zhao State.

units.zh: 封皇弟儉為譙國公，純為陳國公，盛為越國公，達為代國公，通為冀國公，逌為滕國公。
units.en: The emperor's younger brothers were enfeoffed: Yuwen Jian as Duke of Qiao, Yuwen Chun as Duke of Chen, Yuwen Sheng as Duke of Yue, Yuwen Da as Duke of Dai, Yuwen Tong as Duke of Ji, and Yuwen You as Duke of Teng.
units.literal: The emperor's younger brothers—Jian was enfeoffed Duke of Qiao State, Chun Duke of Chen State, Sheng Duke of Yue State, Da Duke of Dai State, Tong Duke of Ji State, and You Duke of Teng State.

units.zh: 世宗明皇帝諱毓，小名統萬突，太祖長子也。
units.en: Emperor Ming, canonically titled Shizong, bore the taboo name Yu and in childhood was called Tongwantu; he was the eldest son of Yuwen Tai.
units.literal: Emperor Shizong Ming, taboo name Yu, childhood name Tongwantu, was the eldest son of the Grand Progenitor.

units.zh: 孝珩破宇文邕，遂至長安，反時何與國家事。
units.en: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?
units.literal: If Xiaoheng defeats Yuwen Yong and then reaches Chang'an, what will rebellion have to do with the affairs of the state?

units.zh: 後周武帝在雲陽，宴齊君臣，自彈胡琵琶，命孝珩吹笛。
units.en: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.
units.literal: Later, when Emperor Wu of Zhou was at Yunyang, he feasted the Qi ruler and ministers, himself playing the barbarian pipa and ordering Xiaoheng to play the flute.

units.zh: 固命之，舉笛裁至口，淚下嗚咽，武帝乃止。
units.en: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.
units.literal: Though pressed he obeyed; he raised the flute barely to his lips, tears falling in sobs, and Emperor Wu then stopped.

units.zh: 後主欲立寵姬張貴妃子始安王為嗣，嘗從容言之，吏部尚書蔡徵順旨稱賞，憲厲色折之曰：「皇太子國家儲嗣，億兆宅心。
units.en: The Later Lord wanted to make the Prince of Shi'an, son of his favorite consort Noble Consort Zhang, his heir, and once mentioned it casually. Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng echoed his wishes and praised the idea, but Xian sternly rebuked him: "The crown prince is the heir of the state, and the hearts of the people rest on him.
units.literal: The Later Lord wished to establish the Prince of Shi'an, son of his favored consort Noble Consort Zhang, as heir, and once spoke of it at leisure. Minister of Personnel Cai Zheng followed his intent and praised the idea, but Xian sternly rebuked him, saying: "The crown prince is the state's reserve heir, on whom the hearts of all the people are fixed.

units.zh: 夏，竟廢太子為吳興王。
units.en: That summer, the crown prince was finally deposed and made Prince of Wuxing.
units.literal: In summer, the crown prince was finally deposed and made Prince of Wuxing.

units.zh: 叔寶肆其昏虐，毒被金陵。
units.en: Chen Shubao gave free rein to folly and cruelty, and his poison spread through Jinling.
units.literal: Chen Shubao indulged his benighted cruelty, and poison spread over Jinling.

units.zh: 數年已來，荒悖滋甚。
units.en: For years his excesses have grown worse.
units.literal: For several years now, wild perversity has grown ever worse.

units.zh: 或微行暴露，沉湎王侯之宅；
units.en: He wanders abroad in disguise, debauching himself in the houses of nobles;
units.literal: At times he goes abroad incognito in revealing dress, drowning himself in the mansions of princes and marquises;

units.zh: 七年，轉光州刺史，上取陳五策，又上表曰：「臣聞夷凶翦暴，王者之懋功；
units.en: In the seventh year he became prefect of Guang Prefecture, submitted five plans against Chen, and memorialized: "I have heard that subduing barbarian violence is the supreme achievement of a true king;
units.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to be prefect of Guang Prefecture; he submitted five stratagems against Chen and also memorialized: "Your servant has heard that cutting down barbarian foes and eliminating the violent is the king's great merit;

units.zh: 或賓士駿騎，顛墜康衢之首。
units.en: or gallops with rowdy companions until he falls in the public streets.
units.literal: or with guest knights and swift steeds he tumbles at the head of the broad highway.

units.zh: 有功不賞，無辜獲戮，烽燧日警，未以為虞，耽淫靡嫚，不知紀極。
units.en: The worthy go unrewarded and the innocent are killed; beacon fires blaze daily yet he feels no alarm; sunk in debauchery, he knows no bounds.
units.literal: Merit goes unrewarded, the innocent are put to death; beacon fires warn daily, yet he is not alarmed; sunk in lust and dissipation, he knows no limit.

units.zh: 牝雞司旦，昵近奸回，尚方役徒，積骸千數，疆埸防守，長戍三年。
units.en: Women rule at court, villains are his intimates, imperial workshops pile up thousands of corpses, and frontier troops serve three-year tours.
units.literal: A hen crows at dawn; he draws close to wicked schemers; convict laborers of the imperial workshops pile up by the thousands; frontier defense keeps men on long garrison for three years.

units.zh: 天厭亂德，妖實人興，或空裡時有大聲，或行路共傳鬼怪，或刳人肝以祠天狗，或自捨身以厭妖訛。
units.en: Heaven rejects his misrule: omens multiply—strange cries in the sky, ghosts reported on every road, livers cut out to appease the celestial dog, men offering their own lives to ward off evil.
units.literal: Heaven loathes chaotic virtue; portents arise and men stir—sometimes great sounds in the empty air, sometimes travelers all report ghosts and monsters, sometimes human livers are cut out to sacrifice to the celestial dog, sometimes men give up their own bodies to appease strange calamities.

units.zh: 民神怨憤，災異薦發，天時人事，昭然可知。
units.en: People and spirits alike are enraged; disasters follow one after another—the judgment of heaven is plain for all to see.
units.literal: The people and the spirits are resentful and angry; disasters and anomalies arise in succession—the signs of heaven and the affairs of men are plainly evident.

units.zh: 後主之世，總當權宰，不持政務，但日與後主遊宴後庭，共陳暄、孔範、王瑳等十餘人，〔五〕當時謂之狎客。
units.en: In Houzhu's reign Zong held power like a chief minister yet did not attend to government affairs; day after day he feasted with Houzhu in the rear court, together with Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang Cuo, [5] and more than ten others. People at the time called them the intimate guests.
units.literal: In Houzhu's reign Zong held power like a chief minister yet did not attend to government affairs; day after day he feasted with Houzhu in the rear court, together with Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang Cuo, and more than ten others. People at the time called them the intimate guests.

units.zh: 〔五〕 共陳暄孔範王
units.en: [5] With Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang
units.literal: [5] With Chen Xuan, Kong Fan, Wang
